rubriker.title: Samarkand R6 (women): China and Kazakhstan remain perfect
rubriker._rss_content: China and Kazakhstan reached the rest day as joint leaders of the Women's Chess Olympiad with perfect 12/12 match scores. Kazakhstan edged Azerbaijan 2½–1½, while China beat Poland 3½–½ after the latter had defeated defending champions India in round five. India responded by overcoming the United States 3–1, while second seeds from Georgia also moved into the chasing group with a convincing win over Uzbekistan. | Pictured: China's Zhu Jiner | Photo: Rafal Oleksiewicz / FIDE

rubriker.title: Six Rounds Down, Five to Go:
rubriker._rss_content: The Chess Olympiad reached its rest day with a settled picture at the top of the Open section and an unsettled one in the Women's, after six rounds that included a world champion's rating milestone, a family reunion on the Swedish board, and a scheduling dispute that ended up saying more about FIDE than about chess.

rubriker.title: FIDE Sets Presidential Candidates Q&A for September 24
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE will host a Presidential Candidates Q&A session on September 24 in Samarkand, giving accredited media a chance to question all three men running for the federation's presidency two days before delegates actually vote. But will all three show up?

rubriker.title: Un proyecto busca acercar el ajedrez a 5.000 niños refugiados
rubriker._rss_content: «Movement in Refuge» busca más apoyo para ampliar su programa de ajedrez destinado a niños rohinyás en Cox's Bazar, Bangladés, después de que un proyecto inicial respaldado por la FIDE llegara a jóvenes refugiados en agosto. La organización benéfica espera recaudar 100.000 dólares para acercar el ajedrez a hasta 5.000 niños más durante los próximos dos años. Su fundador, Magnus Wolfe-Murray, también planea promover la iniciativa en la Olimpiada de Ajedrez de Samarcanda y avanzar hacia el objetivo a largo plazo de formar un equipo juvenil de refugiados.
